{{recipesummary|category=Recipes for dessert|servings=4|time=1 hour, or 2.5 hours|difficulty=3}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United Kingdom|Cuisine of the United Kingdom]]

'''Jam roly-poly''' is a traditional British cuisine probably invented in the early 19th century. It is a flat-rolled suet [[Cookbook:Pudding|pudding]], which is then spread with jam and rolled up. In days past, Jam Roly-Poly was also known as shirt-sleeve pudding, because it was often steamed and served in an old shirt-sleeve. Because of this, another nickname for the pudding was dead-man's arm. Jam Roly-Poly features in Mrs Beeton's cookery book, as Roly-Poly Jam Pudding.

==Ingredients==
* 250 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] or 8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Self-rising Flour|self-rising flour]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 125 g (½ cup or 4 oz) shredded [[Cookbook:Suet|suet]]
* 90–120 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (6–8 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]]) [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] raspberry [[Cookbook:Jam|jam]], warmed
* A little [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]], beaten
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Caster Sugar|caster sugar]] to glaze

==Procedure==
# Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven temperatures|200°C (400°F or Gas Mark 6)]].
# [[Cookbook:Sifting|Sift]] the flour into a bowl with the salt. Add the suet and sufficient water to create a soft but not sticky [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]].
# Turn on to a floured board and [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|roll out]] to a rectangle about 20×30 [[Cookbook:Centimetre|cm]] (8×12 [[Cookbook:Inch|inches]]).
# [[Cookbook:Brush|Brush]] the pastry with the warmed jam, leaving a 1 cm (½ inch) border all around.
# Fold in this border and brush with milk. With the short side towards you, roll up the pastry loosely and seal the ends well. 
# Place on a greased [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|baking sheet]], with the sealed edge underneath. Brush with the beaten egg and sprinkle with caster sugar.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in the oven for 35–40 minutes until golden brown.
# Remove from the oven, sprinkle on a little more sugar and serve hot with home-made [[Cookbook:Crème Anglaise|English custard]].
